speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly where your wrist pain is located and when the fever and skin lesions first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall seeing any tick bites during your camping trip in Minnesota, and can you describe the appearance of the skin lesions? Have you noticed a target-like rash anywhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your hands and wrists are highly characteristic of a specific tick-borne illness endemic to Minnesota. Given your recent travel history and symptoms, I suspect Lyme disease complicated by acute arthritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease
